one_liner: Small ISC-licensed ES5 bytecode interpreter in C for embedding; outscores goja, Boa and Jint on V8 v7, trails Duktape and QuickJS.
what_it_does: MuJS (Artifex, the Ghostscript/MuPDF company) is an embeddable ES5 JavaScript interpreter of about 15,000 lines of C that builds from a single amalgamated one.c. The host drives it through a Lua-style C API: a js_State with a value stack, js_newcfunction/js_setglobal to expose C functions, js_dostring/js_pcall to run code, and userdata objects with finalizers. It is what mpv (meson dependency 'mujs') and MuPDF (Makethird) embed for scripting; it is not a drop-in for goja, Boa or Jint, which are Go, Rust and .NET libraries with their own host APIs.
how_it_is_fast: Its lead over the Go, Rust and .NET interpreters comes from being a plain compiled-C switch-dispatched stack bytecode VM: 16-bit instructions, a tagged-union js_Value on a fixed 4096-slot value stack, interned strings, a dense 'flat' array part for simple arrays, and a stop-the-world mark-and-sweep collector that runs when allocations reach 5x the live set (JS_GCFACTOR 5.0). It does no JIT and has no hidden classes or inline caches: every property access is a strcmp walk of a per-object AA-tree (jsproperty.c), each opcode carries a line-number word, and the loop checks the GC counter on every instruction. That is why Duktape and QuickJS, also C interpreters, beat it.
when_to_use: You need ES5 scripting inside a C or C++ application and binary size matters: the ubuntu CLI binary is 378.8 KB (about 180-260 KB for the library per the project docs), against 2.2 MB for QuickJS.
You want a permissive ISC licence, no build system (compile one.c with any C99 compiler) and no C++ runtime dependency.
Your scripts are glue that calls into C for heavy work; the docs describe a very fast C call-out path and recommend doing the heavy lifting in C.
You are replacing a Go, Rust or .NET JavaScript interpreter (goja, Boa, Jint) with a native one and only need ES5: MuJS scored 1.19x-1.48x goja and 1.56x-1.77x Boa on the V8 v7 suite.
You want the engine already shipped by mpv, MuPDF and the Debian/Ubuntu/openSUSE packages.
when_not_to_use: Raw script throughput matters: Duktape scores 1.09x-1.61x and QuickJS 3.2x-3.5x higher on the same suite and runners, and any JIT engine is one to two orders of magnitude faster.
Your code uses ES2015 or later (let/const, classes, arrow functions, modules, Promises, BigInt): MuJS implements ES5 only.
GC- or allocation-heavy workloads: on ubuntu goja beats it on Splay (1074 vs 818), EarleyBoyer (666 vs 534) and RegExp (271 vs 251), and on macOS goja still wins Splay.

You run hostile scripts and need a hardened engine: the GitHub tracker lists heap-use-after-free (#209, GC during an Array.prototype.sort comparator), heap-buffer-overflows in jsarray.c (#207, #208) and Ap_sort_cmp (#193, #211), all on 1.3.x; earlier CVEs include CVE-2021-45005 (nested try/finally heap overflow in 1.1.3) and an O_getOwnPropertyDescriptor memory-corruption bug fixed in 1.3.2.
Deep recursion or large regex backtracking: the value stack is fixed at 4096 slots and the environment stack at 1024, and the backtracking regex matcher gives up past 1024 recursion levels.

integration.form: source-drop (single one.c amalgamation) or static/shared lib via make release
integration.dependencies: none beyond libc and libm (readline optional for the shell; regenerating utfdata.h needs python3 and the Unicode data files)
integration.min_toolchain: C99 compiler (Makefile uses -std=c99 -pedantic -O3); gcc, clang and MinGW-w64 all build it in the benchmark's CI
integration.platforms: any: Linux, macOS (arm64 tested), Windows via MinGW, Android/iOS and small boards per the docs
integration.thread_safety: not documented; all mutable state lives in js_State (the static sentinels in jsproperty.c and jsintern.c are read-only), so one state per thread with no sharing is the safe pattern

gotchas: Errors use setjmp/longjmp (js_try, js_pcall); a JavaScript exception or error unwinds straight through C++ frames without running destructors, and an error outside any protected call runs the panic handler and then abort() unless the panic function longjmps out.
A regex whose backtracking exceeds REG_MAXREC (1024) does not match slowly; js_regexec returns -1 and the script gets a thrown Error 'regexec failed'.

The GitHub repository is a stub since 2025-08-13 ('Migrate to Codeberg'); the 1.3.8 code measured here lives on codeberg.org/ccxvii/mujs, and many GitHub memory-safety issues (#206-#211) were closed as completed on 2026-03-31 with no linked commit, so check the Codeberg history for the fixes before pinning a version.
Allocation sizes are int (js_Alloc takes int size); arrays are capped at 64M entries (JS_ARRAYLIMIT) and strings at 256 MB (JS_STRLIMIT).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick MuJS over Duktape when you want the smallest, simplest ES5 C engine with an ISC licence and a Lua-like stack API, and you can live with roughly 1.1-1.6x lower V8 v7 scores (Duktape won even when built -Os). Pick QuickJS instead when you need modern JavaScript or about 3x more interpreter throughput and can afford a 2 MB binary; pick MuJS over goja only when the host is C or C++ rather than Go.
verified_claims_summary: On ahaoboy/js-engine-benchmark, a daily third-party GitHub Actions run of the V8 v7 suite (8 benchmarks, in-process timing after a warm-up, geometric-mean Score), MuJS 1.3.8 built with the stock Makefile (-O3, runner default cc) scored 435 / 522 / 339 on ubuntu / macos-arm64 / windows against goja 365 / 358 / 229, Boa 279 / 302 and Jint 246 / 239 / 159 (about 1.2-1.5x goja, derived from page data). The runners' CPU models and compiler versions are not stated, each engine runs once per day, and the same table puts Duktape (682 / 842 / 371) and QuickJS (1522 / 1672 / 1105) ahead of MuJS on every platform.
status_note: Actively maintained by Artifex on Codeberg (1.3.8 is the version built in the benchmark's daily job; the GitHub mirror stopped at 2025-08-13), ISC-licensed and small enough to vendor as one C file, but treat it as unsafe for untrusted scripts given its steady stream of fuzzer-found memory-safety bugs.
